title: Is using the desktop version of Claude/Chatgpt better than using just the web version to make better looking games?
author: The_only_F
selftext:
I'm interested in using AI to help me develop games, but I'm wondering whether using the desktop app versions of Claude or ChatGPT offers any advantages over using them directly in a web browser.

Would the desktop versions actually help me create better-looking games, with better graphics, animations, environments and overall visual quality? 

I tend to just try make prototype games directly putting the commands on the web version they are okay not bad but not amazing. I'm just wondering would I need apps such as Blender + Game Engine and allow the AI to have access to my entire PC to make better quality games?

comments.author: Outrageous-Issue9722
comments.body: Probably, I didn't even know there was a web version. I've had no issues with the desktop app.

replies.author: HEXAPONG
replies.body: You didn’t know you could use Claude through a web browser?

replies.author: Outrageous-Issue9722
replies.body: Nope. Never had a reason to.

comments.author: kultcher
comments.body:
I've been building stuff in Godot.

Recently switched to the Claude desktop app and was surprised to discover that it could run it's own local copy of Godot to test and collect screenshots for verification. It couldn't download Blender directly, but I was able to just send it the Blender installer for Linux and it was able to install and run it afterward. It produced a bunch of Blender assets using Python scripts. By no means are they AAA quality but they're good enough for my modest projects.

Codex can do the same, even from the browser, so I assume Claude probably can too. But I definitely have found that they produce better results when they can actually see their work in the game world and refine it based on that.

comments.author: Time_Cat_5212
comments.body:
The desktop app is, IMO, the superior of the 3 interfaces for most uses.

Browsers and CLI tools have limitations that a desktop app does not.

comments.author: ZymzAlchemy
comments.body: Codex (ChatGPT app) desktop app is the same as the cli tool functionally but provides a better and more organized workspace for people who’d rather work inside a GUI or are uncomfortable in the terminal.

comments.author: DigitalDustChan
comments.body: The web app is nice to start. The desktop app will work directly on your computer, so it takes more work off your plate. Eventually your attention becomes the bottleneck, so anything you can do to optimize that is golden.

comments.author: Ball_Analytics
comments.body:
Yes, 

so I personally use claude-code or codex from the terminal, prefer them cause I've been using them from there from day, (Linux) 

the chatgpt app and claude app have the app friendly desktop version of them which just access your repo in the same way.

Chatgpt you just change from chatgpt to codex and pick your repo folder

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
I've used Codex through the official app, used it as an extension inside of VSCode and used it in the broswer. 

The output quality is identical. You do not get a superior method with any method.

The difference is purely which interface you're most comfortable using.

comments.author: M4xs0n
comments.body: The app versions are directly working in your project and can make changes on its own. The browser version can‘t. That alone should answer your question.

replies.author: The_only_F
replies.body: This is a vague answer it really does not, I was already aware the desktop version can do that but it does not necessarily mean it would make it better.

replies.body: Oh alright boss, if you say so. Why ask the question then if you know the answer?

replies.author: The_only_F
